outcome: A stale or rotating credential stops masquerading as network weather: a dispatch that would die on an expired token is refused up front with a named CREDENTIAL_STALE before any try burns, an auth-class failure from a native CLI is distinguishable from transport on every durable surface, and a credential rotated mid-dispatch by ordinary host use no longer discards the completed work it raced.

HTTP-adapter credentials (API keys carry no expiry vocabulary; the HTTP status mapping already distinguishes auth at internal/driver/http.go:272-286)
runtime park policy (the named codes flow through existing failure surfaces; no new park class)

acceptance.text: Native credential preflight: at dispatch preparation, a credential whose expiry has passed is refused CREDENTIAL_STALE - a named code new to the vocabulary (internal/driver/invoke.go admission set) - before the conversation starts, consuming no try. Today the credential is opaque bytes end to end: expiresAt is parsed nowhere (the only occurrence in the tree is the certification fixture synthesizing it, internal/driver/native_capture_linux.go:758-780), and the per-dispatch gate checks only identity and path (nativeRuntime, internal/driver/native.go:445-462). A file without a parseable expiry passes preflight unchanged - absence of the field is never a refusal. Pinned by driver tests over fresh, expired, and expiry-less credential fixtures. Evidence basis: sworn#221 - a stale overnight OAuth token burned three tries as PROVIDER_TRANSPORT_FAILED and parked the run; a daytime retry with the rewritten file succeeded immediately.

Auth-class is distinguishable on the native path: a CLI run that fails because its token is expired or unauthorized surfaces distinctly from transport failure, instead of collapsing onto the same PROVIDER_TRANSPORT_FAILED as a socket reset (the terminal classification at internal/driver/native_linux.go:2226-2239 today; the CLI's own auth signal is structurally discarded because stderr is a leak check and unparsable stdout is NATIVE_SURFACE_INVALID). The distinction must respect the surface discipline - derived from observable process facts or admitted event vocabulary, never by loosening the leak or surface guards. Pinned by native fixture tests.

Benign rotation stops discarding finished work: a credential rotated by ordinary host use while a dispatch holds its lease - an atomic rename, meaning a new inode at the same path - no longer fails the completed dispatch CREDENTIAL_IDENTITY_CHANGED at lease close (internal/driver/credentials_linux.go:75-96; fired at native_linux.go:2108-2112). Rotation to a valid same-shape credential is recorded loudly and the dispatch's work survives; genuine tampering signals (mode, owner, link-count drift) keep failing exactly as today. Pinned by lease tests over rotation and tampering fixtures. Evidence basis: telemetry-foundations r4 - a captain dispatch was discarded at close because the operator's interactive host use refreshed the subscription token mid-flight.

constraints: Fail-open on ignorance, fail-closed on knowledge: preflight refuses only what it can positively read as expired; unparseable or expiry-less credentials dispatch exactly as today. A preflight false-positive that blocks a healthy dispatch is a worse defect than the status quo.

The credential file's security posture is untouched: 0600, owner, single link, O_NOFOLLOW, the exclusive lease, and the leak scan all stay; A3 relaxes only the close-time identity conclusion for a verified benign rotation.
Check evidence belongs in the submission's checks field, never in files added to the repository.
